posts.name: Bolt
posts.cooked:
I agree with you.

  • The UI before Blizzard removed addons, without addons, was not good enough.
  • The UI after Blizzard has removed addons, is not good enough
  • Several improvements should be made to the UI
    • Post fight analysis tools, you shouldn’t need to /wcl every time
    • Ability to see CC / CDs on enemy unit frames when used
    • A borderline photo copy of Gladius, but restricted in movement
    • Increasing or decreasing / muting specific sounds. I don’t really care about hearing auto attack occur 500 times. I don’t care about hearing Frostbolt, or auto shot or moonfire. I do care about hearing Combustion, or w/e major offensive CD is being pressed. Give me a way to mute rotational garbage, and highlight or emphasize the already in game sounds from abilities.
    • Better ability to see the game, I need my camera not to clip through ceilings, remain stable, and allow me to zoom out more.
    • A party interrupt tracker, and a unified cc type tracker. This has been a point of contention in PvE for over a decade. Overlapping kicks in uncoordinated groups is tragic & borderline unavoidable with how fast casts are.

The UI currently needs work, but I remain under the belief that this is not their final iteration of what they want the UI to be.

I agree with you.

  • The UI before Blizzard removed addons, without addons, was not good enough.
  • The UI after Blizzard has removed addons, is not good enough
  • Several improvements should be made to the UI
    • Post fight analysis tools, you shouldn’t need to /wcl every time
    • Ability to see CC / CDs on enemy unit frames when used
    • A borderline photo copy of Gladius, but restricted in movement
    • Increasing or decreasing / muting specific sounds. I don’t really care about hearing auto attack occur 500 times. I don’t care about hearing Frostbolt, or auto shot or moonfire. I do care about hearing Combustion, or w/e major offensive CD is being pressed. Give me a way to mute rotational garbage, and highlight or emphasize the already in game sounds from abilities.
    • Better ability to see the game, I need my camera not to clip through ceilings, remain stable, and allow me to zoom out more.
    • A party interrupt tracker, and a unified cc type tracker. This has been a point of contention in PvE for over a decade. Overlapping kicks in uncoordinated groups is tragic & borderline unavoidable with how fast casts are.

The UI currently needs work, but I remain under the belief that this is not their final iteration of what they want the UI to be.

Edit*
Oh look, someone else tried to give you the explanation too:

The Beta surprised me

I guess what I am trying to say is I, and a lot of other people in all the WoW pillars say that addons are a big double edged sword and it sucked at how mandatory and how solved they made the game feel. Blizzard is trying to course correct and we all can recognize it’s not perfect by any means, but I wouldn’t call it not listening to the community.

The Beta surprised me

Like I said they have an objective, a North Star, what have you - players will look at what they’re doing and go you all didn’t achieve anything you wanted to, but from their perspective this is just an initial iteration, a place to start. There will be more UI updates, more API pruning, just as they’ve been tuning classes for 25 years.

For a programmer there’s no such thing as failure, there’s just a lesson learned and the next iteration. There’s no way to discover exactly what needs to be done until you release something and see how it works in practice. It’s how we are trained to work because it creates software that’s guided by the real world instead of dropping huge designs that takes years and years to make and then end up gigantic failures. Blizzard’s API and UI changes are just small failures they can course correct.

At least, that’s my view. WoW also has a gigantic mountain of tech debt and the bugs and crashes you see are more a product of trying to rapidly change a system made up of new pieces and pieces that have been modified for 25 years. The instance infrastructure is full of issues I’ve heard. Their UI required lots of refactorings just to make edit work in Dragonflight. Lot’s of parts of the UI that were never designed to be customized or work the way ElvUI works because it’s written from the ground up in an extensible way.

That and the fact that it seems like they’ve cut a lot of QA and are trying to churn out releases and content at a faster pace than ever before. Maybe they’re even experiment with LLMs now. Every tech company I know of is secretly trying to generate code to create velocity even if they don’t say it publicly.
